title: Five Second Talking Face Swap
tests: Tests a short video face swap with source identity, temporal consistency and original audio preserved, without misrepresenting free-tier capabilities.

judge.summary: The five-second output consistently resembles the portrait and preserves the kitchen and framing, with no conspicuous facial artifacts in the supplied frames, though exact motion preservation and lip-sync cannot be verified.

must_haves.item: The delivered video is 5 seconds long and follows the first 5 seconds of talk-one.mp4.
must_haves.why: The output is confirmed as five seconds long and uses the original scene, but only one source frame is supplied, so correspondence to the original first five seconds cannot be fully verified.

must_haves.item: The woman's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg throughout, rather than reverting to the original face between frames.
must_haves.why: All four output samples consistently resemble the portrait, with matching facial features and dark curly hair; none visibly revert to the original woman.

must_haves.item: The original kitchen, body motion and framing remain; her hair and clothing may follow the portrait so she is recognisable.
must_haves.why: The kitchen layout and camera framing are preserved, and the permitted hair and clothing changes match the portrait. Exact preservation of body motion cannot be checked against a single source still.

must_haves.item: Original speech is audible and synchronized with the video.
must_haves.why: The supplied sound report confirms audible speech, but neither the original audio nor a timed audiovisual sequence is available to establish unchanged speech and synchronization.

must_haves.item: The face remains aligned during mouth and head movement, without conspicuous flicker or doubled facial features.
must_haves.why: The sampled frames show a coherently aligned face across different mouth shapes and head positions, without visible doubling or obvious facial distortion.
